observations: Shot 1 (0.00-0.12s sampled, 'New pump, going in'): real ASZ technicians fitting the red fire-pump unit at a pipe joint, faces visible (owner-approved 25 Oct 2026), audible on-site sound. Matches the caption and visible action truthfully; no false claim of a finished or tested system.

Shot 2 (1.94-3.76s sampled, 'Team at work, pump room'): same team continuing to work on the fitting, one additional person partially in frame at left edge. Matches caption; framing is clean with no visible old branding/captions from any prior edit.

Shot 3 (4.00-7.76s sampled, 'Step by step, installation' and transition to pan): covers the end of the team's visible work and the camera's genuine pan up and away from the people toward the overhead pipe corner by ~7.4-8.0s. I independently re-timed this boundary (the asset library previously, incorrectly, carried this scene as extending to 16.0s; corrected to 7.2s/8.0s this run after frame-by-frame inspection) -- the manifest's shot timings were built against the corrected boundary, so the rendered shot genuinely matches 'installation' work, not an unrelated static pipe shot mislabelled as people-work.

Shot 4 (8.00-18.73s sampled, two 'Step by step, installation' / 'Pump room, taking shape' shots): overhead galvanized pipework at a wall corner with scaffolding below, no people, no client name/address/signage visible anywhere in the sampled frames. This is a genuinely static-leaning hold in the source footage (confirmed by direct frame inspection at 1s increments through the full clip), not a rendering fault; the two shots from this scene look similar because that is what the camera actually recorded. The final shot carries the 'assafetyzone.com' CTA text per the standard last-shot template.
